feedback: The confession follows the already available distinction between the photographed toast and Mona's false sealed-water story. It confirms taking poison at the preview and putting it in the waiting glass, but neither fact supplies a new mechanism needed to solve the case. Her closing concern about having betrayed the claimants is emotionally stronger than her original commission embarrassment alone. Monet and Chip's parallel admissions help explain why their document lies remained suspicious without making them killers. I found the result earned, though the confession's explicit explanation of why she substituted water repeats the inference I had just made; a little less explanation there would leave more emotional space.
